note: Linear tweens, in milliseconds. A swap is a SPEED — `swapMsPerCell` times the straight-line distance the pieces travel, floored at `swapMinMs` so a one-cell swap is still visible; any two cells can be swapped, so that distance runs from 1 to about 8. `holdMs` is a still beat after each phase; `staggerMs` delays each piece by how far it sits from whatever fired, so a shoved run reads as a wave rather than a block; `splitBeats` plays a step's movement and its destruction as two beats. `glyphFadeMs` is how long the piece takes to go, which is shorter than the cell it sat on: the glyph leaves as the ability fires and the ground keeps turning without it. `fx` is what an ability throws: a `throw` beam leaves and dissipates over `reachCells`, a `grab` beam reaches out over `reachMs` and then holds whatever it caught. `ghost` is the outline a glyph with no beam swells out of itself: a small pulse when it swallows something and holds its place, a big one when it matches and goes. `grow` is how much a plain piece swells as it fades. `spin` is how a cell being destroyed turns as it shrinks away: `turns` of them, on a curve of `ease` — 1 is a constant speed and higher starts slower. `easing` names the curve each tween runs on: `move` for a piece travelling, `shrink` for a cell being destroyed — the parameter is what bends, so the turn stays inside the footprint the shrink has made for it. `hitStopMs` lengthens the beat that ends where an ability fires, so a landing registers as an event rather than a frame. `escalate` builds the chain: `per` is how much louder each further link plays and `cap` is the link past which it stops growing. `flash` is the bloom a landing throws, white under screen so every colour lifts the same fraction of the headroom it has left: `spread` in cell widths, `falloff` how sharply it goes. `burst` is what a cleared cell throws: `count` dots of `sizePx`, out to `speed` of a cell and slowing over `settle` of their `ms`, fading by `fade`, spread by `scatter`. Its `ms` cannot outlast the beat the cell dies on, which is `shrinkMs` plus `holdMs`: the beat is where `since` is measured from, and a longer burst is cut off rather than finished. `swapArc` bows a swapped piece off its straight line, in cells, so the two pass either side of each other. `smear` is the copies a swapping piece leaves behind it: `copies` of them, `spacing` of its travel apart, and only above `minCells` of distance. `squash` narrows a travelling piece along its heading to `floor` of its width and widens it across by whatever holds its area. `jiggle` answers a swap that set nothing off: the two cells shake for `ms` at a constant `deg`, `cycles` times, shrunk to `scale` to make room to turn in. `finaleHoldMs` is how long the board sits empty between a won level going and the next one growing in. `shake` moves the board on a landing: `px` at the first link, over `ms`, decaying by `decay`. Tune in dev/timing.html.
